units.title: 1. Structural Myopathies, Dystrophin Defect, DMD Timeline and Becker
units.guide:
Dystrophin defect is structural protein involvement with necrosis of muscle replaced by adipose and fibrous tissue, X linked deletion and steroid treatment; the photograph is captioned lordosis.
Duchenne's muscular dystrophy is progressive muscle degeneration with a 0-18 year timeline: gross motor delay (walking late), frequent falls presenting to clinic, toe walking with Gower's sign, cramps unrelated to exercise and lordosis, supported walking, wheelchair bound, upper limb involvement and finally respiratory involvement with aspiration pneumonia as the m/c cause of death.
Additional involvement covers scoliosis leading to ILD, pseudohypertrophy (calf > other muscles), mental retardation, cardiomyopathies and nocturnal hypoventilation leading to pooling of secretions and aspiration. Becker's is milder: cardiac death (dilated cardiomyopathy), CK/EMG/biopsy similar to DMD, presentation 5-60 years, survival >40 years, contracture absent, less weakness and mental retardation absent.

units.title: 2. Limb Girdle, Emery Dreifuss, Facioscapulohumeral, Oculopharyngeal and Myotonic Dystrophy
units.sec: LGMD, EDMD, FSHD, OPMD & Myotonic Dystrophy
units.guide:
LGMD is autosomal dominant/recessive, the m/c adult onset muscle dystrophy, associated with cardiomyopathy, involves lamin and caveolin and shows the diamond on thigh sign (vastus medialis hypertrophy with atrophy of other muscles); photographs show winging of scapula in LGMD.
Emery Dreifuss is X-linked recessive/autosomal dominant with prominent contractures and cardiomyopathy. FSHD is autosomal dominant with muscle asymmetry, proximal upper limb plus distal lower limb involvement and B/L ptosis with facial muscle involvement.
Oculopharyngeal is autosomal dominant with ptosis, ophthalmoplegia and dysphagia. Myotonic dystrophy is autosomal dominant trinucleotide repeat disease of chromosome 19 with DM1 > DM2 and proximal lower limb plus distal upper limb involvement with myotonia; photograph shows hatchet facies.

units.title: 3. Myotonic Dystrophy Presentation and Metabolic/Mitochondrial Myopathies
units.guide:
Hatchet facies combines ptosis, temporal hollowing (temporalis), elongated face and facial muscle involvement; investigation shows percussion myotonia with contraction on repeated percussion and failure to release.
Associated findings are cardiac conduction abnormalities, mental retardation, gonadal atrophy, insulin resistance, SNHL and posterior subcapsular cataract; photographs show percussion myotonia, B/L winging of scapula and humeral atrophy with winging.
Mitochondrial myopathies are maternally inherited with ragged red fibers on trichrome stain and exercise induced weakness/fatiguability/cramps. CPEO gives ptosis + ophthalmoplegia without dysarthria or diplopia and is a D/D for NMJ disorders (myasthenia gravis). Kearns Sayre syndrome is CPEO before 20 years with retinitis pigmentosa, complete heart block and cerebellar ataxia; MERRF and MELAS complete the list.

units.title: 4. Channelopathies and the Periodic Paralyses
units.guide:
Channelopathies show an LMN pattern of acute onset, B/L symmetrical, episodic motor weakness with electrolyte imbalance as D/d.
Calcium channel diseases (mnemonic E2 S6 HOm) are episodic ataxia type 2, spinocerebellar ataxia type 6, hypokalemic periodic paralysis and familial hemiplegic migraine; sodium gives hyperkalemic and normokalemic periodic paralysis and paramyotonia congenita; chloride gives myotonia congenita; potassium gives Anderson-Tawil syndrome, episodic ataxia type 1 and benign neonatal familial convulsions on day 5 of birth.
Hypokalemic periodic paralysis is autosomal dominant, adolescent, m > F, precipitated by a high carbohydrate meal, with pure proximal limb weakness, propensity for arrhythmias and hypokalemia during episodes; treatment is oral potassium and acetazolamide. Hyperkalemic periodic paralysis and Anderson-Tawil syndrome share AD inheritance, childhood (1st decade) onset and episodic weakness; hyperkalemic PP has myotonia (+), K+ may be normal, worsening by cold and precipitation by rest, whereas Anderson-Tawil has no myotonia, variable K+ and dysmorphic facies with arrhythmias.
